itineraries.title: Dawn After the Don - 7 Day Itinerary
editorial: Our week in Colombia was mostly spent in Medellin and Cartagena, with a brief stop in Bogota. In all honesty, unless raucous parties are your jam, Cartagena is skip-able. Between the hawkers and the humidity, it’s a rather unpleasant experience.
What if we had more time?
We do regret picking Cartagena over the Cocora Valley, most notable for its coffee plantations and the tallest palm trees in the world. It would have added another 3 days to our itinerary.

days.title: Day 1 - Medellin
editorial: We set up base in the upscale Laureles neighbourhood, which felt residential but not sleepy. We loved to concept of small grocery stores doubling up as street-side cafes in the evening.

Before sunset, we walked from Laureles to the hilltop Pueblito Paisa, which houses a replica Antioquian village. The panoramic city views in the setting sun are worth the visit, so go by cab if you don’t fancy the short (and safe) hike.

days.title: Day 2 - Medellin
editorial: The day of the Don. We did the Pablo Escobar tour, which really put in perspective how impressive Medellin’s transformation has been in the last three decades.

From the most dangerous city on Earth, it had become one of the most liveable cities we’ve encountered on our travels. The brick facade buildings (”incomplete” constructions to avoid tax) and tree lined streets create a uniquely beautiful atmosphere. Medellin was one of the greenest cities we’ve visited, living up to the “City of Eternal Spring” moniker.

days.title: Day 3 - Guatape
editorial: Day three was a day trip to Guatape, which is a 2.5-hour bus ride away.

The main town is a visual delight with it’s building decorated with colourful panels (called zócalos). After satiating our desire for pretty pictures, we climbed El Peñón, a giant granite rock. There is no elevator, so you’ll have to trudge up 740 steps.
The views from the summit of the rock are absolutely breathtaking, with water turquoise lagoons and little islands spreading in every direction.

days.title: Day 4 - Medellin + Cartagena
editorial: On our final day in Medellin, we traversed Comuna 13, an erstwhile slum that has become a cultural hotspot notable for it’s vibrant street art.
In the afternoon, we flew to Cartagena, where we felt the climate and the culture change.
Cartagena feels distinctly Caribbean compared to the Hispanic Medellin. The music, the food, and even the colonial streets feel like it could be in the West Indies.
After sundown, Cartagena is one big party!
Oh, and for the best experience, get a place in Getsemani.

days.title: Day 5 - Cartagena
editorial: Before the weather got brutal, we explored the cobbled streets and colourful buildings of the old town.
We tried to walk down to a beach in the modern Bocagrande neighbourhood, but only made it as far as a mall before turning around due to the oppressive heat.

Unfortunately, the heat wasn’t the only thing affecting our experience. The aggressive behaviour of hawkers around tourist areas is very very tiresome. If you don’t believe, read any of the Google Reviews of popular hotspots.
We abandoned our plans of visiting nearby islands, as the hawker menace is worse there since the tourists are literally trapped on the islands until their boats’ return ferry.
Afternoons in Cartagena are for siestas, but you can step out again in the evening to walk around.

days.title: Day 6 - Cartagena
editorial: Finally, we walked along the Walls of Cartagena, 11 kms of stone fortifications built some 300 to 500 years ago to protect against the pirates of the Caribbean.
We also explored the Castillo San Felipe de Barajas, a 17th century fortress.
In the evening, we returned to the Walls for the sunset views. The setting sun, the sea breeze, and the old stone made for our most memorable moments in Cartagena.

days.title: Day 7 - Bogota
editorial: We flew into Bogota in the early morning for a flight later in the evening.
The capital felt cooler, denser, and grittier than Medellin. We spent our brief time in Plaza de Bolivar, the main square of the country.
